Body shape and maximum size in the Slender armourhead (Pentaceros wheeleri) reflect a robust, deep-bodied morphology typical of pentacerotids, with recorded individuals attaining an ultimate total length of 44 centimeters [Li = 44 centimeters] in field surveys conducted around seamounts of the South Pacific. This species exhibits a relatively compressed body form with strong dorsal spination, features that are believed to aid in predator deterrence during benthic foraging. Morphometric data from commercial bycatch collections indicate that puberty, as determined by gonadal recrudescence and the onset of vitellogenesis in females, is reached at a total length of 28 centimeters [Lp = 28 centimeters]. This length represents a significant threshold in the species’ life cycle, marking the transition from an immature, predominantly growth-oriented phase to one involving reproductive investment. Comparative analyses with congeneric Pentaceros species suggest that this size at maturation is intermediate, reflecting a trade-off between the energetic demands of reaching a large adult body size and the advantages of early reproductive output in a variable deep-sea environment.

Field collections of mature females during the pre-spawning period, carried out at a stable water temperature of 7.8 °C [T = 7.8 °C], yielded a gonadosomatic index (GSI) of approximately 9.8% [GSI = approximately 9.8%]. This value indicates a moderate allocation of somatic resources toward gamete production, consistent with an iteroparous reproductive strategy in which energy is partitioned across multiple spawning seasons rather than concentrated into a single, exhaustive event.

The earliest developmental stages of Pentaceros wheeleri are characterized by a small initial body mass that imposes substantial mortality risks during the pelagic larval phase. Estimates of wet weight at birth, derived from egg dimensions averaging 1.1 millimeters in length and 0.6 millimeters in width, produce a computed value of 0.00021 grams [Wwb = 0.00021 grams] under the assumption of an ellipsoidal egg morphology. This minute birth mass, among the lowest recorded for pentacerotid fishes, dictates that the yolk-sac larva must rely entirely on endogenous yolk reserves during the first several days after eclosion. The duration of this yolk-dependent period is tightly coupled to ambient temperature; at the local thermal regime of 7.8 °C [T = 7.8 °C], the interval from chorion rupture to first exogenous feeding is approximately 3.5 days [ab = approximately 3.5 days]. This relatively rapid yolk absorption relative to other temperate marine teleosts may reflect selection for early feeding onset in an environment where planktonic prey availability is patchy and seasonally variable.

Body mass at reproductive maturation provides an important physiological link between somatic growth and the onset of breeding activity in this species. Using the length–weight relationship parameterized from extensive fishery samples, the mass corresponding to the length at puberty of 28 centimeters yields an estimated wet weight at puberty of 453 grams [Wwp = 453 grams]. This value suggests that females must accumulate substantial somatic reserves before allocating energy toward vitellogenesis and spawning, a pattern commonly observed in long-lived demersal fishes occupying oligotrophic seamount ecosystems. In contrast, the ultimate wet weight for males, derived from the same length–weight relationship applied to the maximum recorded total length of 44 centimeters, reaches approximately 1765 grams [Wwi = approximately 1765 grams]. Males thus achieve a considerably larger body mass than the pubertal threshold, indicating a growth trajectory that continues well after the onset of reproductive maturity, a pattern that may be linked to intrasexual competition for spawning opportunities or to size-dependent fecundity advantages in females.

Longevity estimates for the Slender armourhead point to a relatively extended lifespan for a teleost of its body size, which is consistent with the slow life-history pace typical of deep-sea benthic fishes. Under the prevailing thermal conditions of 7.8 degrees Celsius, the maximum documented lifespan is 4015 days [am = 4015 days], equivalent to approximately 11 years, as inferred from otolith increment analysis of specimens collected from the Louisville Ridge seamount chain. The combination of a protracted juvenile period, a modest reproductive output per event, and a long reproductive lifespan positions Pentaceros wheeleri as a typical K-selected species within its benthic fish assemblage.
